gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns an unjustified use of a common sample count m and an i.i.d. equal-count hypothesis when invoking the Monte Carlo error theorem. ISSUE-001 instead concerns applying an RKHS boundedness proposition outside its function-space hypotheses in the Sobolev invariance theorem; it does not recognize the sample-count assumption or the failed theorem invocation in the gold issue.

The gold issue is the invalid inference from an upper bound on the smallest Gram-matrix eigenvalue to an upper bound on its reciprocal, requiring instead a lower spectral estimate. ISSUE-003 diagnoses a separate quotient-rule simplification error in a density derivative and its resulting constant; it does not address eigenvalue direction, reciprocal control, or the Wendland amplification estimate.
